own_scenes.place: Nueva York y Long Island (Calliope Studios)
own_scenes.desc: Seis meses antes de Straight Outta Compton, los Jungle Brothers (Mike Gee, Afrika Baby Bam, DJ Sammy B), criados con jazz y pioneros en meter house en el hip hop, sacaron Straight Out the Jungle (1988); en «Black Is Black» aparecía su compañero de instituto Q-Tip, a quien Baby Bam puso el nombre. Si N.W.A vestía chaquetas de los Raiders, ellos iban de safari: afrocentrismo, alegría y sampleo de jazz, Bob James y grooves de R&B. De La Soul (Posdnuos, Trugoy y Maseo, del instituto de Amityville) mandó «Plug Tunin’» a Prince Paul de Stetsasonic, que la llevó a Tommy Boy. En un concierto en Boston en 1988 los grupos se reconocieron y nació el colectivo, con Queen Latifah, Monie Love, Black Sheep y Chi-Ali: los estudios Calliope eran «una comuna hippie» y el remix de «Buddy» su primer posse cut. 3 Feet High and Rising (1989) cambió James Brown por un collage de decenas de samples, sketches y chistes internos (hoy en el Registro Nacional de Grabaciones); «Ladies First» de Latifah y Monie Love se volvió un himno para generaciones de mujeres. A Tribe Called Quest (Q-Tip, Phife Dawg, Ali Shaheed Muhammad, Jarobi) fichó por Jive: People’s Instinctive Travels and the Paths of Rhythm (1990) y The Low End Theory (1991), jazz y hip hop superpuestos, limpiados por el ingeniero Bob Power, con Phife convertido en compañero de pleno derecho y la frase «record company people are shady» (que Jive puso en camisetas). Q-Tip, perfeccionista del SP-1200, fichó al joven J Dilla de Detroit. Abrieron el camino a Outkast, Kanye West o Pharrell: «la libertad de hacer lo que quieras».

refs.para: They fed off one another’s creativity, while inspiring groups like Black Star, Dilated Peoples, the Pharcyde, and legions of others. Their defining trait was joy. The songs, sound, and lyrics were Afrocentric, and their vibe arced toward the positive and good-natured. They introduced the genre to wide-ranging sampling. And if N.W.A was at home wearing black Starter jackets with Raiders logos, groups like Jungle Brothers were just as comfortable in their khaki safari gear.
refs.chapter: Cap. 11: Like Coachella in the Studio

refs.q: Calliope Studios was a big hippie commune.
refs.para: Monie Love (artist, London): Calliope Studios was a big hippie commune. And that was the existence of the Native Tongues. When I think about it now, I’m surprised we didn’t have tents in the studio. There’s always somebody at the console tinkering away at a beat or somebody at the sampling machine, sampling something.
refs.chapter: Cap. 11: Like Coachella in the Studio

refs.q: I have to write something that is going to outshine everything that I’ve heard already. For the simple reason that I have to do better because I’m a woman.
refs.para: And I sat in there for maybe an hour, hour and a half. And the pressure in my head was there. Like, I have to write something that is going to outshine everything that I’ve heard already. For the simple reason that I have to do better because I’m a woman. It can’t be mediocre. I have to write something memorable that’s going to stick out, that everybody’s going to repeat.
refs.chapter: Cap. 11: Like Coachella in the Studio

refs.q: Every day was like Coachella in the studio.
refs.para: Monie Love (artist, London): Every day was like Coachella in the studio. Whenever we performed all together—Jungle, De La, Tribe, Latifah, throw in some Black Sheep—that was an official festival vibe on stage. The legacy of us is we allowed people to feel good about being themselves, and not having to conform to any specific type of role because you’re in hip-hop. Our legacy really spells out freedom. Freedom in the music genre to do what you want.
